author: Penry Buckley and Lisa Cox
description:
Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.

After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.
title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation

author: Sophie Sullivan
description:
Democrats – including incoming banking chair and both majority leader candidates – said wealthy interests were prioritized over the needs of working Americans

In response to a Guardian investigation, four US Senate Democrats say they will work to resurrect a financial watchdog agency that has abandoned dozens of enforcement actions under the second Trump administration.

The Guardian found that after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) dropped more than 20 lawsuits against banks and corporations accused of a range of financial misconduct, complaints against those firms rose by an average of more than 75%. In many of these recent complaints, consumers described the same issues the CFPB’s suits had sought
title: ‘Worth fighting for’: senators vow to restore financial watchdog agency after Guardian investigation

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Controversial Colorado Republican narrowly lost House seat in midterms but says ‘I’m not mad at the president’

Lauren Boebert says Donald Trump “did some things that hurt” her constituents before they voted the pugnacious Colorado Republican out of her US House seat during midterm elections, which saw her and the president’s party lose control of Congress.

“This could be a referendum on President Trump,” Boebert said to the Associated Press in an interview published on Friday. “It could be the referendum on Congress or the Republican party. I think it’s all of it.

Continue reading...
title: Lauren Boebert says Trump ‘did some things to hurt’ her constituents

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness

A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States.

Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.

Continue reading...
title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die

author: Marina Dunbar in New York
description:
Eva Yi Xie was taken into custody at Washington DC airport after presenting research at neuroscience conference

A Princeton University doctoral student has reportedly been taken into custody by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after traveling to Washington DC, for a neuroscience conference.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year PhD candidate at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute, was detained Thursday at a Washington-area airport, according to university officials and her colleagues.

Continue reading...
title: Princeton doctoral student reportedly detained by ICE on way back from conference

author: Reuters
description:
Nikhil Gupta admitted to plotting with Indian government official to hire hitman to murder dual US-Canadian citizen

An Indian ⁠man was sentenced to more ⁠than 19 ​years in US prison on Friday after admitting to orchestrating a failed Indian government-backed plot to kill a Sikh separatist in New York ⁠City, in connection with what US and Canadian authorities have called a broader effort to target Indian dissidents.

Nikhil Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy ⁠to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Continue reading...
title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York

author: Guardian staff and agencies in Copenhagen
description:
Russian intelligence thought to be behind plan to kill US-Ukrainian musician Kyivstoner before concert in Denmark

Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper.

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark,”, Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. The expulsion will happen within seven days.

Continue reading...
title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged Moscow link to attempted killing of rapper

author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
description:
The pair had flown from the Scottish Gliding Centre at Portmoak on a training flight

Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning.

Police Scotland said their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Two men killed after glider crashes into Loch Leven in Scotland

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Young’s abusers were convicted through suspect-centric prosecution, though much more needs to be done for victims

Hope can be found in the darkest of places. Joanne Young stood outside Winchester crown court on Thursday and said she was relieved – not just for herself and her family – but for women in the future.

Young, who was subjected to years of drugging and rape by her husband, who invited other men to assault her, waived her anonymity to speak out.

Continue reading...
title: Joanne Young’s faith in justice system is sign of real change, but courts are still catching up

author: Kevin Rawlinson and Aisha Down
description:
News of vulnerability comes after retailers in at least seven European countries hit by cyber-attacks

A secret government cybersecurity operation recently warded off the risk of a cyber-attack on fridges and freezers in UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums, it has emerged.

An attack would have been similar to those that have caused many millions of euros of damage in continental Europe in recent months. But, while many retailers have now been protected, researchers warned that many more could still be vulnerable.

Continue reading...
title: UK operation wards off risk of cyber-attack on supermarket fridges and freezers

author: Ed Pilkington
description:
Reinaldo Dennes screamed in pain and took over an hour to die – but Texas officials branded the execution a success

A botched execution in Texas on Thursday night that lasted more than an hour and caused the prisoner to scream out, begging the Lord to end his suffering, has led to renewed calls for a nationwide moratorium that would pause all lethal injections.

It took 63 minutes for Reinaldo Dennes, 70, to be proclaimed dead in the Huntsville penitentiary. The execution team had struggled to find a vein through which a lethal dose of the sedative pentobarbital could be administered.

Continue reading...
title: Latest botched execution prompts calls for US moratorium on lethal injections

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Zacharia’s spokesperson called allegations she falsely represented herself as an attorney ‘baseless’

  • US politics live – latest updates

Katie Zacharia, the former White House press secretary hired and fired in the same week, is under investigation by the state bar of California for claiming to be a lawyer despite never passing the bar exam.

Earlier this month, the state bar of California informed Campaign for Accountability, a non-profit watchdog group, that it had assigned an investigator and legal adviser to investigate Zacharia after the
title: Fired White House press secretary Katie Zacharia under California state bar investigation

author: Associated Press
description:
Reinaldo Dennes’ execution took more than an hour as workers struggled to find suitable veins

An observer of the botched execution of Texas prisoner Reinaldo Dennes this week has said the effects of the lethal injection were like nothing he’d ever seen before.

The execution of Dennes at the Huntsville unit of the Texas department of criminal justice took more than an hour as the team managing the procedure struggled to find suitable veins in which to administer the injection to the prisoner.

Continue reading...
title: Onlookers say botched Texas prison execution is like nothing they have ever seen

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
Duo’s fame set to soar after Pattinson announced as next James Bond – but they will take newgen approach to power

He is the next James Bond. She is a successful model/actor/singer-songwriter. Together, they are set to become the next big British power couple in Hollywood.

This week Robert Pattinson and Suki Waterhouse, who have been in a relationship since 2018, were thrust into the global spotlight after the news that he had landed arguably the biggest and most glamorous role in film.

Continue reading...
title: Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson to become Britain’s next big Hollywood power couple

author: Steven Morris
description:
Relatives speak out as inquest jury finds Alice Webb’s death after filler entered her organs was accidental

The family of a woman who died after a botched Brazilian butt lift have called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys” to be introduced before more people lose their lives.

Speaking as an inquest jury concluded Alice Webb’s death was accidental, her family said they were astonished people were still having BBLs despite what had happened to her.

Continue reading...
title: Bring in ‘cosmetic cowboys’ law to avoid more deaths, says family of butt lift victim

author: Maria G Ortiz-Briones
description:
A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union

Hundreds honored and celebrated the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta this week with a series of public events including a vigil and celebration of life in Bakersfield.

Huerta, a feminist icon who co-founded the United Farm Workers (UFW) in 1962, died on 28 October aged 96.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A source of inspiration’: series of public events celebrate life of Dolores Huerta

author: Anne Davies
description:
The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.

This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.

Continue reading...
title: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: the teals

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Federal judge in Colorado finds immigration officials in contempt but takes no more action after they end practice

A federal judge said that the US Immigration and Customs ⁠Enforcement agency (ICE) “made a mockery of court orders” in Colorado and that the court found government officials in contempt ⁠for instantly re-arresting a ⁠man whom ​the judge had ordered released.

US district judge Charlotte Sweeney declined to take any further action because she ⁠said the officials had “cured the contempt by ceasing the practice at issue” as sworn by an official in court.

Continue reading...
title: Judge says ICE ‘made a mockery of court orders’ with instant re-arrest policy

author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
description:
Warnings over exploitation risks come amid push for investigation into supported exempt accommodation sector

The home secretary has launched an attack on providers of housing for vulnerable residents in her Birmingham constituency, saying she “smells a rat” after warnings over spiralling costs and risks of exploitation.

It comes amid a push for an independent investigation into the supported exempt accommodation (Sea) sector in Birmingham, one of the largest in the country.

Continue reading...
title: Mahmood ‘smells a rat’ over housing provision for vulnerable people in Birmingham

author: Peter Walker, Jennifer Rankin and Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Discord between EU and UK on whether arrangements for food and drink, emissions trading and youth mobility scheme depend on settlement for students

The UK and EU have agreed a reset deal, Downing Street has said, although the level of tuition fees EU students will pay to study at UK universities remains unresolved.

“The deal is done – negotiations have concluded,” a No 10 statement said, less than an hour after the prime minister, Andy Burnham, arrived at the summit venue in Brussels, where he was greeted by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, and António Costa, the European Council president.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham has agreed EU reset deal with tuition fees issue unresolved, says No 10

author: Martin Belam
description:
Record-breaking IPO for company behind Claude comes amid tumbling prices for other AI stocks. Plus why the humble potato could be vital for future space missions

Good morning. Global stock markets have slumped as Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a sell-off in AI-linked companies. The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by over 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO.

The blockbuster debut easily places Anthropic’s IPO as the biggest in history, with the 980m shares sold raising $81bn, surpassing the previous record. According to reports, demand for Anthropic shares was about six times what the company was able to offer. US economic growth is inextricably tied to the booming AI sector, and in particular the vast investments in datacentres that power programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT.
title: First Thing: Blockbuster Anthropic IPO fails to halt global slide in AI stocks

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Report based on survey of 20,000 Americans says 84% of people who are incarcerated were assaulted, shot or stabbed

The majority of people who have spent time in a US prison or jail have, at one point in their lives, been a victim of a violent crime, according to a new study. Researchers with Just Safe, a victims’ advocacy non-profit, found that 84% of people who had been incarcerated reported being assaulted, shot or stabbed before their first time in jail or prison.

The report is based on a nationally representative survey of 20,000 Americans. Of those who have been incarcerated, half of them had been hurt by a caregiver as a child and one-third were victims of sexual or intimate partner violence.

Continue reading...
title: Majority of people who have been in US prisons were also victims of violent crime, study finds

author: Sam Levine
description:
Former Trump lawyer urged justice department officials to seek pardons for those falsely claiming he won the 2020 presidential election in their states

In the fall of 2025, Cleta Mitchell, a key lawyer in Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election, contacted a justice department official with an urgent request.

Criminal cases against people who signed certificates falsely claiming that Trump won the presidential election in their state – known widely as fake electors – were pending in Georgia, Michigan, Arizona, Nevada and Wisconsin. She knew the official, pardon attorney Ed Martin, was working on a memo outlining why those involved in the fake elector scheme should receive a presidential pardon.

Continue reading...
title: Emails reveal how Trump allies pushed pardons for election deniers

author: José Olivares
description:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Perez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike

The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”

A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Perez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Traumatizing’: hunger striker in ICE detention tells of force-feeding ordeal – and what made him crack

author: Mark Sweney
description:
State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors

California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

Continue reading...
title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China

author: Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
description:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mo
title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

author: Jamie Grierson, Emine Sinmaz and Helena Horton
description:
Woman who waived anonymity says she hopes her case will mean other victims of abuse are more likely to come forward

A woman who was drugged and raped by her husband and strangers he had invited to their family home has been praised for her bravery in exposing the crimes.

The judge in the case and women’s rights advocates said Joanne Young’s courage had been a feature of the trial. Her decision to waive her anonymity and attend court has seen her likened to Gisèle Pelicot, who was drugged and raped by her husband as well as dozens of strangers in France. Waiving her right to anonymity, Pelicot said shame “must change sides”.

Continue reading...
title: Joanne Young praised for bravery in exposing rape by husband and strangers

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Exclusive: While PM pushes for EU reset, Tory leader is moving away from ‘divisive’ issue that defined party for years

  • UK-EU summit live: latest news updates

Kemi Badenoch has been advised by her team to limit the amount of time she spends discussing Brexit and Europe, the Guardian has been told, moving the Conservatives away from an issue that defined the party for many years.

While the Tory leader still gives views on Brexit – in an opinion piece in the Daily Mail on Thursday she condemned Andy Burnham’s ongoing reset with the EU as a “backwards” move – sources say it
title: Senior Tories urge Badenoch to drop Brexit talk in major strategy shift, sources say

author: Catie McLeod
description:
NSW health issues public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas

Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials have said.

NSW health on Friday issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.

Continue reading...
title: Vape users hospitalised after losing consciousness, prompting public health warning in New South Wales

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
Inquest into the deaths of four babies after free and home births hears routine checks and follow-up may have saved their lives

Four babies who died in New South Wales – three after free births and one after a home birth – might have survived if they had had routine checks and follow-up , a coronial inquest has heard.

Baby DH, Baby D, Baby R, and Baby B died in the state’s northern rivers region betw
title: Baby born with heart abnormalities ‘didn’t have a chance’ after non-medical free birth, NSW inquest hears

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor
description:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

Conti
title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers

author: Ali Aziz, Maria Talal and Tom Levitt
description:
Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists

The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy.

As many as 400 women are estimated to have joined protests over the past two weeks calling for the return of their professors at Al-Qadisiyah University in a move that appears to have surprised its administrators.

Continue reading...
title: Iraq university’s removal of male professors teaching women sparks weeks of protests

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Exclusive: Investigation launched after details of grief and trauma uploaded, raising questions over extent of issue

The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) has launched an investigation after a patient was “horrified” to discover that notes of sensitive discussions with her psychotherapist had been shared with more than 100,000 NHS workers.

Rosanna (not her real name) found out that her detailed therapist’s notes, including about her grief and trauma, had been uploaded to her patient records when she saw them on a computer screen during a visit to her GP.

Continue reading...
title: Patient ‘horrified’ to find her sensitive discussions were shared with more than 100,000 NHS staff

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in February 2024

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon knew he had murdered two men and his attempts to explain the disposal of their bodies “ring completely hollow”, a court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon’s explanations of body disposal ‘ring hollow’, court hears

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Public expectations around datacentres have changed in the age of AI, chief executive Craig Scroggie says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Community backlash to a datacentre expansion in inner Melbourne that resulted in NextDC’s share price dropping 40% will change the way the company engages with communities – and it says it will no longer pursue new developments near homes.

The company held its first annual general meeting since it was forced to delay the controversial expansion of its M3 site in West Footscray after power provider Jemena paused construction o
title: NextDC vows to keep future datacentres away from homes after community backlash in Melbourne

author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Polly Hudson, produced by Ruth Abrahams, Saskia Collette, Eleanor Biggs, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Homa Khaleeli
description:
After Russell Brand’s conviction and accusations against David Walliams, campaigners are calling for a staggered age of consent. Nosheen Iqbal speaks to the columnist Polly Hudson and the educator Michael Conroy about what needs to change

Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com

Anger, disgust, shame. In the last couple of weeks, as news of famous older men being convicted and accused of crimes against very young women and girls has emerged, the public mood has shifted.

The conversation has moved from “how did society let this happen?” to “how do we stop it from happening again?”. In that space, a campaign has grown for the consent gap to be closed.

Continue reading...
title: Is it time to change the UK age of consent? – podcast

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Sean Cairncross exits after outages that sparked fierce criticism, with DoD official Kirsten Davies to take over

White House national ⁠cyber director Sean ⁠Cairncross ​was ousted from his job, a person close to the White House told Reuters on Thursday, ⁠days after tech outages hit US air travel, banking and national security systems.

Cairncross oversaw cybersecurity policy and ⁠strategy across the federal government. Department of Defense chief information officer ​Kirsten Davies will ‌assume the position ‌temporarily, according to the source.

Continue reading...
title: White House cyber director ousted after US hit by wave of tech outages

author: Associated Press
description:
A federal judge ruled that messages sent by Brooke Rollins to USDA workers suggest Christianity is a shared faith and violate the first amendment

Religious messages that US agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins emailed to the agency’s 100,000 employees were unconstitutional, and she must be careful to avoid proselytizing when communicating with workers, a federal judge ruled Thursday.

Rollins sent the messages, which included Christian messages and images, from her official email account on holidays such as Independence Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter. She did not send messages commemorating holidays from other religions.

Continue reading...
title: Religious messages agriculture secretary emailed to staff deemed unconstitutional

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Independent National Security Legislation Monitor says reference to religion has ‘contributed to discrimination and violence against religious minorities’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Religion should be removed from Australia’s terrorism definition and making bomb threats should not result in life imprisonment, the country’s national security laws watchdog has said.

The highly anticipated report from the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor (INSLM), released Thursday, reviewed how terrorism has been defined in Australia over the past 25 years after a suite of laws were introduced following the September 11 attacks in the United States.
title: Religion should be removed from terrorism definition under Australian law as it gives ‘false credibility’, watchdog says

author: Ben Doherty in New York
description:
Congressional Budget Office also questions whether Australian-flagged vessels could be compelled into a conflict with China under Aukus deal

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Providing nuclear-powered submarines to Australia would diminish the US navy’s own fleet for “many years”, a new report for the US Congress has cautioned, questioning whether Australian-flagged vessels could be compelled into service in a conflict with China.

The US navy’s latest shipbuilding plan does not countenance the Aukus agreement in its forecasts at all, noting only in a footnote that the transfer of any Virginia-class submari
title: US warned supplying nuclear-powered submarines to Australia would diminish its own fleet for ‘many years’
